A reviewer can read which module was delegated, what the sub-agent reported back, and how the lead integrated it, then jump from the matching commit to the same session through its checkpoint. The sub-agent reports in the transcript are labelled as model output, not user instructions. **The interactive-hook problem and its resolution.** The `prepare-commit-msg` hook asks "Link this commit to session context? [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways". From the non-interactive agent shell, that prompt waits forever. Commit `a86ab8d` was completed only after the stuck hook process was stopped, so it has no checkpoint trailer; `entire doctor` looked healthy, which hid the cause. The resolution recorded in `evidence/entire/README.md`: answer `a` once in an interactive terminal so the choice is remembered. After that, `70400f8` and `75783c2` carry trailers. ### 5.3 cfo.ai (business plan) **The plan** (shared model: https://cfo.ai/s/LuzFz_Xw5PkfkLJJ, horizon October 2026 to September 2027; exports in `evidence/cfo-ai/`; assumptions in `evidence/cfo-ai/dealscope-assumptions.md` and `assumptions.md`). All of it is assumption: DealScope has no customers, no revenue and no signed pilots (stated in the investor summary PDF and the assumptions brief). **Pricing options compared.** Per audit at $750, $1,500 or $3,000; an annual deal-team plan at $24,000 including 24 audits with $1,000 per extra audit; a hybrid of a $6,000 workspace fee plus $1,000 per audit. No unlimited plan until data-cost variance and support load are measured. **Unit economics.** Delivery cost of $94.65 per audit = 1.5 hours of human QA at $60 ($90), plus $2.60 of Crustdata (26 credits x $0.10 per credit, the per-credit price being an editable input because it is not published), plus $0.05 of LLM inference, plus $2 tooling. Card processing at 3% and support sit below gross profit. Fixed costs are $750 per month ($150 hosting, $100 software, $500 sales and marketing) plus $500 per month compliance from month 6. Founder salary is a $0 placeholder. **Three scenarios** (`evidence/cfo-ai/DealScope-investor-summary.pdf`): | | Conservative | Base | Growth | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Earned revenue (12 months) | $30,000 | $270,000 | $390,000 | | Audits delivered | 40 | 180 | 390 | | Gross margin | 87.20% | 93.69% | 90.54% | | Contribution margin | 82.20% | 90.02% | 86.79% | | Peak modeled funding need | $1,500 | $0 | $0 | Conservative assumes 2 customers x 2 audits per month at $750 with data and model costs 50% higher and a two-month delay to first revenue. Base assumes 5 customers x 3 audits per month at $1,500. Growth assumes a linear ramp to 15 customer-equivalents x 4 audits per month on annual pricing; its $555,000 of collections includes $165,000 of deferred service obligations that are not earned revenue. **Runway is left blank** because opening cash was not supplied, and the model deliberately did not invent a number; a zero funding need does not mean cash is available. The margins are dominated by the assumed $90 of human review per audit, so they say little about the data and model cost. **How real run data fed back.** - *Crustdata credits per audit.* The plan used 26 credits (a pre-run estimate: 4 enrichments, 2-3 people searches of 25 results, jobs search). Measured actuals from the two traced live cases were 9.18 (Retool) and 12.21 (Airtable); the corrected Notion run recorded 4.82 (the log does not explain the lower figure). At the same $0.10 per credit assumption, 9.18-12.21 credits is $0.92-$1.22 rather than $2.60, which would lower delivery cost by roughly $1.38-$1.68 per audit (our arithmetic), under 2% of the $94.65 total. The measured figures are not yet written into the cfo.ai export, which still carries 26 credits, so the modeled data cost is conservative (`SUBMISSION_EVIDENCE.md`, `evidence/cfo-ai/assumptions.md`). The investor summary's statement that 200 credits cover about 7 audits at 26 credits or 5 at the 40-credit cap uses the estimate, not the measured numbers. - *LLM cost.* The plan assumed $0.05 per audit (about 6 model calls, roughly 40k input plus 5k output tokens). neatlogs showed about $0.003 per planner call and $0.0015-$0.02 per synthesis call, in total of the order of a few cents per audit by our reading of the screenshots. Free-tier runs were billed $0. The $0.05 input is therefore about right in order of magnitude and could be replaced by a measured figure. - *What this changes.* Little of the margin story, because human review dominates. It does change the data-credit capacity of the 200-credit allocation, and it shows that the per-audit price of data is the least certain input (it depends on the per-credit price, which we did not obtain). --- ## 6. Limitations and next steps **Limitations (honest).** - Small samples. Four live cases and two synthetic scenarios, n = 1 per experiment variant. Nothing here validates the signals as predictors of deal outcomes; thresholds are heuristics. - Public-profile coverage is a sample, not a census. S2, S3 and S5 depend on how many profiles Crustdata returns and whether they carry dated employment intervals; the 25-result cap deepens this. - Provider data discontinuities exist and only the loosest guard is in place (section 3). - The baseline-versus-improved experiment showed no difference in unsupported claims; it showed improvement in verified-claim count only. The improved-variant memo is larger partly because deterministic findings are merged in, which is not purely a prompt effect. - The deployed LLM runs were on a free tier with a daily quota, so several runs used fallback paths; model identity varied across runs. - The Retool trace is missing from the neatlogs dashboard because of an ingest outage. - There are no customers, no revenue and no external validation; the cfo.ai plan is a set of hypotheses. Runway is blank because cash is unknown. - Pending items listed as TODO in `SUBMISSION_EVIDENCE.md` when this was written: demo video, public `#neatHack` post URL, quote-post submission URL, confirmation of the final deadline, an Entire screenshot and an `entire-graph`. - Several evidence files contain statements that are now stale and should be reconciled before submission: `README.md` ("Proof pending" under Partner tools), `evidence/entire/README.md` (header "Status: TODO"), `evidence/neatlogs/successful-run.md` and `failure-recovery.md` ("screenshots TODO", though 13 now exist), and `SUBMISSION_EVIDENCE.md` ("Screenshot paths: TODO" for neatlogs). We did not edit those files. **Next steps (suggested, not committed work).** - Re-export the cfo.ai plan with measured credits and measured LLM cost and a real per-credit price. - Run a few more live cases with a paid or higher-quota Gemini key to compare LLM versus rule-based planning with enough runs to say something. - Add a human review step to the UI (the business plan already assumes 1.5 hours of QA per memo). - Run design-partner pilots with agreed accuracy and usefulness criteria, as the investor summary proposes. - Replace the regex-style verifier heuristics with additional deterministic checks and a held-out set of adversarial claims. --- ## 7. # neatlogs: baseline vs improved

Status: measured 2026-10-11. Raw results: `baseline-vs-improved-20261011T144412Z.json` (scenario A) and
`baseline-vs-improved-20261012T102646Z.json` (scenario B, re-run after a budget-pool bug fix). Command:
`python scripts/run_case.py --deterministic-planner --model gemini-3.1-flash-lite eval --scenario <a|b>`.

## Design
- Same synthetic fixture, same deterministic (rule-based) investigation for both variants, so the only difference
  is memo synthesis: **baseline** = loose "summarize the risks" prompt, memo contains only the Gemini draft (the
  verifier still runs; its *draft* metrics show what a verifier-less system would have published); **improved** = strict evidence schema, observation/interpretation separation, mandatory
  alternative explanations, prohibited-claim rules, plus deterministic findings, all gated by the verifier.
- Model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite (free-tier daily quota on gemini-3.8-flash and 3.6-flash was exhausted; see log).
- Metrics are computed by the deterministic verifier on the Gemini draft (pre-publication) and on the published memo.

## Results (n = 1 run per variant per scenario — small sample)

| Scenario | Variant | Trace id | Draft claims | Draft rejected | Draft verified / qualified | Grounded rate | Published claims | Tool calls | Runtime |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | baseline | `28fe5ba00882582eb3d298795274dff9` | 4 | 0 | 2 / 2 | 1.0 | 4 | 7 | 4.5 s |
| A | improved | `4475d391852dad1707054011b73a3d11` | 6 | 0 | 5 / 1 | 1.0 | 15 | 7 | 5.0 s |
| B | baseline | `39ee81cc2045fe5f160e428bb24943cd` | 3 | 0 | 1 / 2 | 1.0 | 3 | 8 | 16.1 s |
| B | improved | `e63bac7e90a7d4de175c300f139a82a2` | 6 | 0 | 6 / 0 | 1.0 | 17 | 8 | 15.2 s |

Simulated Crustdata accounting for each scenario-A run: 20.25 credits (synthetic pool; no real credits spent).

## Honest reading
- **No reduction in unsupported claims was observed**: the baseline prompt produced 0 rejected claims on both
  fixtures, because the model only sees the evidence index (with IDs) in both variants.
- Observed differences: the improved variant produced more claims that pass verification outright (5 vs 2 on A;
  5 vs 2 on B), a lower share of qualified (single-source / missing alternative explanation) claims on A, explicit
  diligence questions, and a fuller memo once deterministic findings are merged.
- The verifier's rejection behaviour is demonstrated separately by unit tests and by
  `test_unsupported_llm_claims_are_rejected_from_memo` (fabricated ID, "40% left", IP-leak and valuation claims all
  rejected).
- Scenario B was re-run on 2026-10-12: the first B run (`superseded/baseline-vs-improved-20261011T144435Z.json`)
  was invalid because simulated (synthetic) credit spend from earlier demo runs had been counted against the live
  account-wide cap, so some tool calls were blocked (GLOBAL_SPENDABLE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED). Fixed: the global cap now
  applies to the live pool only; synthetic runs keep their per-case cap.
- Superseded attempt (`superseded/`): first eval run on gemini-3.6-flash hit 503/429 errors so neither variant got
  an LLM draft; it is kept for transparency, not used as a result.

17:**Result of the live tests (all figures from `IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` and `evidence/neatlogs/`).** We ran four paid live cases against real Crustdata data (plus one fully cached re-run) with a real Gemini planner. Retool (`case-8ddc70b2b4de`) used 9.18 credits and scored risk 22.2 with 92.5% coverage. Airtable (`case-289f654e60f5`) used 12.21 credits, scored risk 42.7 (Watch), coverage 92.5%, evidence confidence 90, and its regenerated memo had 14 claims, 13 verified and 1 qualified, 0 rejected. A first Notion attempt using `notion.so` spent credits and returned no usable evidence because the domain is ambiguous in Crustdata; that failure led to a free identity pre-check. The corrected Notion run (`notion.com`, `case-d60a330a199c`) used 4.82 credits, scored risk 32 (Watch), coverage 92%, confidence 87. Total real Crustdata spend recorded was 36.21 of 200 credits. In the live runs whose verification results are recorded (Retool, Airtable, the cached Notion re-run) the verifier rejected nothing from the published memo; in the controlled baseline-versus-improved experiment the model's drafts also contained no unsupported claims, so we cannot claim the verifier removed bad claims in live data (see section 5.1). These are small-sample demonstrations on a handful of public companies, not validation of the signals as predictors of anything.
94:4. The run completed in 4 planner turns with 36 evidence records and 4.82 Crustdata credits actual: risk 32 (Watch), coverage 92%, confidence 87, neatlogs trace `b3875a81576975a4536e4bf132c8c7bb`.
97:The log does not say why this run spent 4.82 credits against 9.18 and 12.21 for the earlier cases. One possibility is reuse of peer enrichments cached from the failed first attempt, but that is not stated, so we draw no conclusion from the difference.

Synthesis calls range from $0.0015 on gemini-3.1-flash-lite at 2,175 tokens (`213426.png`) to $0.02 on gemini-3.6-flash at 11,146 tokens for the live Airtable memo regeneration (`213710.png`), which made no new tool calls. The cfo.ai plan had assumed $0.05 per audit. (Costs are neatlogs list-price figures read from screenshots; actual billing on the free tier was $0, per `evidence/cfo-ai/assumptions.md`.)
169:- *The Input/Output improvement.* Early traces had blank Input/Output columns; after the fix each root span reads, for example, "complete (planner_stop); risk insufficient evidence; coverage 30%; tool calls 1; verified claims 10" (`213426.png`).
180:**Honest reading.** There was no reduction in unsupported claims: both variants had zero rejected claims on both fixtures, because the model only sees the evidence index with IDs in either case. The improved variant produced more claims that pass verification outright (5 versus 2 on both scenarios), a lower share of qualified claims on A, explicit diligence questions and a fuller memo once deterministic findings are merged. The verifier's rejection behaviour is shown separately by unit tests (for example `test_unsupported_llm_claims_are_rejected_from_memo`: a fabricated ID, a "40% left" claim, an IP-leak claim and a valuation claim are all rejected), not by this experiment. A first evaluation attempt on gemini-3.6-flash hit 503/429 and gave neither variant an LLM draft; it is kept under `evidence/neatlogs/superseded/` and not used.

The investor summary's statement that 200 credits cover about 7 audits at 26 credits or 5 at the 40-credit cap uses the estimate, not the measured numbers.
